newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso checks slide as dlr short-cover wanes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso checks slide as dlr short-cover wanes.

text.p: The Mexican peso recouped some ground lost earlier against the dollar at the close of trade on Thursday as speculation and dollar short-covering eased, traders said.
"The market opened with dollars in demand to cover shorts. Nonetheless, after the peso weakened to 7.92 per dollar, it picked up a little," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 2.4 and 1.6 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9100/7.9130 and 7.8980/7.9010 per dollar.
"Some brokers bought dollars in speculative deals, but began to sell long positions when they saw the peso was not about to weaken further," another trader said.
Traders said dealers had covered short dollar positions early on to hedge against a possible selloff in U.S. long bonds after the release of U.S. producer price data on Friday morning.
"The market is closely following the long bond and U.S. economic data," a dealer said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 1/32 in late trade to yield 7.11 percent.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 1.9 centavos weaker at 7.9000/7.9040 per dollar.
